root_cause.text: The bridge's `br_nd_send()` function assumed that the Neighbor Discovery (ND) option area in the received packet's skb was linear, but the callers only guaranteed linearity of the ICMPv6 header and target address, causing potential out-of-bounds access when parsing options from a non-linear skb.
root_cause.evidence: The commit message states: "br_nd_send() parses neighbour discovery options from ns->opt[] and assumes that these options are in the linear part of request. Its callers only guarantee that the ICMPv6 header and target address are available, so the option area can still be non-linear." The patch adds `skb_linearize(request)` and re-derives the `ns` pointer from the linear network header after linearization.
